story: On Magnolia Loop in Sumter Oaks, this sunny Monday afternoon at 4:17, Gary is scanning the street bulletin board for an Architectural Review approval notice for his cart lights and sound system, while Hal and Rosa stand by with sketches in hand. Hal makes it clear that nothing gets bolted onto any cart until the committee posts its approval, and Rosa offers to walk the drawings over to the committee herself so everyone is ready by Saturday. Meanwhile, over at the Rec Center, Donna is studying the ladder standings with determination, working out how many wins she'll need to pass Pruitt-Kowalski.
events: Gary (street bulletin board): Scan for an Architectural Review approval notice on my cart lights and sound system
Donna (ladder standings board): Study the ladder standings to see how many wins we need to pass Pruitt-Kowalski

gary.thought_process: I filed the Architectural Review application back at tick 156 and the bulletin board still hasn't turned up an approval notice. Rosa and Hal are both here, and Hal already said he'll look at Rosa's sketches after his flamingo count. I shouldn't keep pestering anyone about the parade. What I can do is check the board myself, since I'm standing right here, and see if Review posted anything or if there's an update about the parade. That's the useful thing before I touch my cart wiring. Rosa is reading the board too, so I might get some conversation out of it naturally afterward.

parameters.content: Scan for an Architectural Review approval notice on my cart lights and sound system

donna.thought_process: I'm at the Rec Center with no one around, so no one to recruit Gary in person right now. The ladder standings board is right here, and I want to see exactly how far Pruitt-Kowalski is ahead of us so I can tell Gary how many wins we need. Checking the board is a productive step toward my pickleball goal while I wait for Gary to finish at the bulletin board.

parameters.content: Study the ladder standings to see how many wins we need to pass Pruitt-Kowalski

hal.thought_process: Rosa asked me to look over her cart sketches once I finished the flamingo count. Both she and Gary are at the bulletin board checking for an Architectural Review notice, so this is a natural moment to settle things. My notebook is the unofficial conscience of the street, so I'll do this by the book: nothing gets built until Review signs off, and the flamingos stay at three. I'll answer Rosa directly instead of repeating my earlier line, and keep Gary honest at the same time. The leftovers are a fair trade, though I'll deny it if the committee asks.

parameters.content: Count's done, Rosa, so show me those sketches. If Review hasn't posted anything yet, nothing gets bolted on until they do. Same goes for you, Gary.

rosa.thought_process: Dinner went well, and Hal said he'd look at my cart sketches after his flamingo count. I already asked him, so I shouldn't push again. Gary is checking the bulletin board for an Architectural Review notice, and I read the flyer last tick without seeing one. The practical next step is to ask Gary directly what he found, since the parade is Saturday and the carts can't be built until Review signs off.

parameters.content: Gary, did you spot a Review approval on the board? I didn't see one earlier. If it's not up yet, I'll walk the sketches over to the committee myself so we're ready by Saturday.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
